calculation_handling.description: Measurement rule: the number of required loading spaces is worked out from the total gross floor area on the lot. It states the basis, not a value.

Measurement rule for multi-unit industrial buildings in the Employment Industrial Zone category: loading spaces are based on the interior floor area of each industrial unit, not the whole building. Industrial buildings are outside the residential building types we model.
calculation_handling.gaps: The Employment Industrial zone category is not in the residential zone vocabulary.

calculation_handling.description: Definition of an industrial unit: the part of a building used or controlled by one owner or tenant, for calculating Chapter 220 loading spaces.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies to industrial buildings, outside the residential building types we model.

calculation_handling.description: Exclusion rule: interior floor area of an industrial unit used only for mechanical, electrical, stair, elevator, atrium, basement storage, parking or loading purposes does not count as gross floor area for loading space calculations.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies to industrial units, outside the residential building types we model.

calculation_handling.description: A required off-street loading space must stay available for the use it is required for. This is an operating obligation with no value to compute.
calculation_handling.gaps: No requirement token in the vocabulary fits an ongoing availability duty.

units.disclosure: A required off-street loading space has to remain available for the use that needs it. We do not test this.

calculation_handling.description: Loading spaces inside a building must be clearly marked and identified. This is a marking obligation with no value to compute.
calculation_handling.gaps: No requirement token in the vocabulary fits a marking duty.

units.disclosure: Loading spaces inside a building must be clearly marked and identified. We do not test this.

calculation_handling.description: In Policy Area 1 (PA1), a required loading space for a building with no dwelling unit needs at least 4.4 m of vertical clearance, despite the dimensions in 220.5.1(8).
calculation_handling.gaps: The Policy Area 1 map is not held, and the no-dwelling-unit test has no condition token.

calculation_handling.description: Type A loading space: minimum length 17.0 m, width 3.5 m, vertical clearance 4.4 m. Only the clearance has a target.
calculation_handling.gaps: The vocabulary has no loading-space length or width target, so 17.0 m and 3.5 m are not expressed.

calculation_handling.description: Type B loading space: minimum length 11.0 m, width 3.5 m, vertical clearance 4.0 m. Only the clearance has a target.
calculation_handling.gaps: The vocabulary has no loading-space length or width target, so 11.0 m and 3.5 m are not expressed.

calculation_handling.description: Type C loading space: minimum length 6.0 m, width 3.5 m, vertical clearance 3.0 m. Only the clearance has a target.
calculation_handling.gaps: The vocabulary has no loading-space length or width target, so 6.0 m and 3.5 m are not expressed.

calculation_handling.description: Type G loading space: minimum length 13.0 m, width 4.0 m, vertical clearance 6.1 m. Only the clearance has a target.
calculation_handling.gaps: The vocabulary has no loading-space length or width target, so 13.0 m and 4.0 m are not expressed.

220.5.1.10(1).explanation: The number of loading spaces a building needs is worked out from the total gross floor area on the lot.

220.5.1.10(2).explanation: For an industrial building with several industrial units in the Employment Industrial zone category, loading spaces are based on each unit's interior floor area, not the whole building's gross floor area.

220.5.1.10(3).explanation: An industrial unit is the part of a building used or controlled by one owner or tenant, for working out loading spaces.

220.5.1.10(4).explanation: Floor area used only for mechanical, electrical, stairs, elevators, atriums, basement storage, parking or loading does not count as gross floor area when working out loading spaces for an industrial unit.

220.5.1.10(5).explanation: A required off-street loading space has to stay available for the use that needs it.

220.5.1.10(6).explanation: Loading spaces inside a building have to be clearly marked and identified.

220.5.1.10(7).explanation: In Policy Area 1, a required loading space for a building with no dwelling unit needs at least 4.4 m of vertical clearance, regardless of the standard dimensions.

220.5.1.10(8).explanation: Loading spaces have minimum sizes by type. Type A: 17.0 m long, 3.5 m wide, 4.4 m clear. Type B: 11.0 m, 3.5 m, 4.0 m. Type C: 6.0 m, 3.5 m, 3.0 m. Type G: 13.0 m, 4.0 m, 6.1 m.
